1.note: Jeremiah begins to record the words of Yahweh here without introducing them with a quote margin such as “Thus says Yahweh.” In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [Thus says Yahweh,]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sin**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [How the people of Judah have sinned]

Here, **Judah** represents the people of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The sin of the people of Judah]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the **sin of Judah** were an inscription that was **being written with a stylus of iron with a point of diamond**. He means that the guilt of the people is permanent and cannot be erased. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is being written permanently and indelibly]

The expression **is being written** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I am writing]

A **diamond** is the hardest stone, and it is the stone that engravers used for cutting into other hard materials. If your readers would not be familiar with what a diamond is, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with an extremely hard stone tip]

The expression **being engraved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which someone engraves]

Even though Yahweh is addressing the people of Judah directly, he is speaking of them in the third person as **their heart** before shifting to the second person in **your altars**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the second person consistently here. Alternate translation: [on the tablet of your heart and on the horns of your altars]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the inner being of the people of Judah were a stone **tablet** on which their sin had been etched. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [permanently into their inner being]

The **horns** of an altar were projections at its four upper corners that were shaped somewhat like the horns of an animal. If your readers would not be familiar with what these were, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and on the corners of your altars]

2.q: כִּ⁠זְכֹּ֤ר בְּנֵי⁠הֶם֙ מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֔⁠ם וַ⁠אֲשֵׁרֵי⁠הֶ֖ם עַל־עֵ֣ץ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן עַ֖ל גְּבָע֥וֹת הַ⁠גְּבֹהֽוֹת
2.note: The word that the ULT translates as **as** indicates that the sin of Judah was being recorded at the same time as when their children were remembering **their altars and their Asherim**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [at the same time that their children remember their altars and their Asherim by the green tree on the high hills]

The implication is that when their children **remember their altars and their Asherim**, they are continuing to worship idols at these places. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [as their children keep worshiping their Asherim at their altars]

The implication is that **the green tree on the high hills** marks the places where the people of Judah worshiped idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [at the idol shrines by the green tree on the high hills]

3.q: הֲרָרִ⁠י֙ בַּ⁠שָּׂדֶ֔ה חֵילְ⁠ךָ֥ כָל־אוֹצְרוֹתֶ֖י⁠ךָ לָ⁠בַ֣ז אֶתֵּ֑ן בָּמֹתֶ֕י⁠ךָ בְּ⁠חַטָּ֖את בְּ⁠כָל־גְּבוּלֶֽי⁠ךָ
3.note: **My mountain in the field, your wealth, all your treasures as plunder I will give, your high places for sin within all your borders** — Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [My mountain in the field, your wealth, and all your treasures I will give as plunder because of the sin you have committed at your high places within all your borders]

3.q: הֲרָרִ⁠י֙ בַּ⁠שָּׂדֶ֔ה חֵילְ⁠ךָ֥ כָל־אוֹצְרוֹתֶ֖י⁠ךָ לָ⁠בַ֣ז אֶתֵּ֑ן
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could change the order of these phrases. Alternate translation: [I will give as plunder my mountain in the field, your wealth, and all your treasures]

The implication is that **My mountain in the field** refers to Mount Zion in Jerusalem, along with the open country around it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Mount Zion and its surrounding countryside]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **plunder**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all your treasures for your enemies to plunder]

The implication is that **your high places** were shrines on the hilltops where the people of Judah sinned by worshiping idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your hilltop shrines where you sinned by worshiping idols]

4.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [since]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And you shall loosen your hand, even yourself, from the inheritance that I gave to you] or [And you shall lose your own control of the inheritance that I gave to you]

Yahweh is using the pronoun **yourself** to emphasize that the people of Judah will themselves be responsible for losing the land. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate this emphasis. Alternate translation: [And you shall loosen, yes, you, from the inheritance that I gave to you]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the land of Judah as if it were an **inheritance** that the people had received from him. He means that he gave them the land as a permanent family possession. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you shall loosen, even yourself, from the land that I gave to you as a permanent possession]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from the land that I gave you to possess forever]
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:14.

5.note: The expression **Cursed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I curse the man]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everyone who trusts in mankind]

Here, **flesh** represents human beings and **his arm** represents his strength. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and who makes people his strength]

Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [and who turns away his heart from me]

Here Yahweh is speaking of a person’s loyalty as if it were his **heart**, which he **turns away** from Yahweh. He means that such a person stops being devoted to Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and who stops being devoted to Yahweh]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5. This also occurs in verses 19 and 21 of this chapter.

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a shrub in the desert** is stunted and lifeless, so is the person who trusts in human beings rather than in Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [For he shall be as stunted and lifeless as a shrub in the desert]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if experiencing something were to **see** it. He means that this person will never enjoy anything good. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he shall never enjoy anything good when it comes]

Yahweh is using the adjective **good** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [when good things come]

The implication is that **a land of salt** is ground where nothing can grow, so no one lives there. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a land so full of salt that nothing grows there, and where no one lives]

The expression **not inhabited** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and where no one lives]

7.q: בָּר֣וּךְ הַ⁠גֶּ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְטַ֖ח בַּֽ⁠יהוָ֑ה וְ⁠הָיָ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה מִבְטַחֽ⁠וֹ
7.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Blessed is the man who completely relies on Yahweh]

The expression **Blessed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh blesses the man]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **confidence**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he is confident in Yahweh]

8.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֞ה כְּ⁠עֵ֣ץ שָׁת֣וּל עַל־מַ֗יִם וְ⁠עַל־יוּבַל֙ יְשַׁלַּ֣ח שָֽׁרָשָׁ֔י⁠ו
8.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a tree which is planted by waters** always has the water it needs to stay alive, so is the person who trusts in Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [For he shall be secure, just like a tree which is planted by waters and by the river, which sends out its roots and always has what it needs]

The expression **is planted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [like a tree which someone has planted by waters]

8.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א ירא כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣א חֹ֔ם וְ⁠הָיָ֥ה עָלֵ֖⁠הוּ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן
8.note: The pronoun **he** refers to any person who trusts in Yahweh, while the pronoun **its** refers to the tree. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and that man does not fear when heat comes, for that tree’s leaf will be green]

8.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א ירא כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣א חֹ֔ם וְ⁠הָיָ֥ה & עָלֵ֖⁠הוּ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן וּ⁠בִ⁠שְׁנַ֤ת בַּצֹּ֨רֶת֙ לֹ֣א יִדְאָ֔ג
8.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [ and he does not worry about dry heat, for plants will retain green leaves and producing fruit]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **fear**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and he is confident]

8.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א ירא & לֹ֣א יִדְאָ֔ג וְ⁠לֹ֥א & יָמִ֖ישׁ מֵ⁠עֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּֽרִי
8.note: This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **cease**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and he will keep on producing fruit]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **anxious**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [he will be calm]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the person who trusts in him as if that person were a tree that could **cease from producing fruit**. He means that this person will continue to prosper. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [nor will he ever stop flourishing]

9.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the thoughts and desires of a person were his **heart**. In this culture the heart was regarded as the place where a person thinks and decides. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A person’s thoughts are deceitful above all things]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **heart**. He means human hearts in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Every human heart]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the corruption of the human heart as if it were a sickness that is **incurable**. He means that no one is able to change it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and no one can change it]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to understand the human heart. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [no one can know it!]

10.note: Here, **heart** represents the thoughts of a person and **kidneys** represents the deepest feelings of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [am the one examining a person’s thoughts, testing a person’s deepest feelings]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [to give to each person according to that person’s ways]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the conduct of a person as if it were the **ways** on which he walks. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to how he has behaved]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the results that a person’s actions produce as if they were **fruit**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to the results of his deeds]

11.q: קֹרֵ֤א דָגַר֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א יָלָ֔ד עֹ֥שֶׂה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְ⁠לֹ֣א בְ⁠מִשְׁפָּ֑ט
11.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a partridge that hatches but did not lay** ends up with young that do not belong to it, so is **the one getting riches but not by justice**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Just as a partridge ends up with chicks that are not its own when it hatches eggs it did not lay, so the one getting riches but not by justice ends up with wealth that is not truly his]

A **partridge** is a kind of bird that nests on the ground. If your readers would not be familiar with what a partridge is, you could use the name of a similar bird that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [Like a ground-nesting bird]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **justice**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [but not in a just way]

Jeremiah is using **in the midst of his days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “when he has lived only half of his life.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the middle of his lifetime]
The pronoun **it** refers to the riches that this person has gained. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [those riches will leave him]

The implication is that when this person dies, everyone will recognize that he has acted foolishly. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and when he dies, everyone will see that he has been a fool]

12.q: כִּסֵּ֣א כָב֔וֹד מָר֖וֹם מֵֽ⁠רִאשׁ֑וֹן מְק֖וֹם מִקְדָּשֵֽׁ⁠נוּ
12.note: Here Jeremiah is speaking of the temple in Jerusalem as if it were **A throne of glory, high from the beginning**. He means that it is the place from which Yahweh rules as king. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Our sanctuary is the exalted place from which Yahweh has ruled as king from the beginning]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:21.

13.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 14:8.

Jeremiah is addressing Yahweh directly as **you**, and in the words **the ones turning away from me** Jeremiah is speaking of himself as the deliverer of messages from Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the second person consistently here. Alternate translation: [all of the ones abandoning you shall be ashamed; the ones turning away from you]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of people who stop being loyal to Yahweh as if they were **turning away from** him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones who stop being loyal to me]

The phrase **The ones turning away from me** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [The ones turning away from you]

The expression **shall be written** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you will write in the earth]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the names of these people were **written in the earth**. He means that they will disappear quickly, just as writing in the dust is soon blown away. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shall vanish quickly]

The word translated as **because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [given that]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of Yahweh as if he were **the fountain of living waters**. He means that Yahweh is the source of life for his people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the source of life]

14.note: Here Jeremiah is speaking of being rescued from his troubles as if it were being **healed** from a sickness. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Deliver me from my troubles, Yahweh, and I shall be delivered]

The expression **shall be healed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I will become well]

The expression **shall be saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I shall truly be secure]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **praise**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the one whom I praise]

15.note: Jeremiah is using the term **Behold** to focus Yahweh’s attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Please pay attention]

The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Judah who oppose Jeremiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [my opponents among the people of Judah are saying to me]

These people are using the question form to mock Jeremiah because the disaster he announced has not yet happened. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [The word of Yahweh is nowhere to be seen!]
See how you translated this phrase in 8:9. This also occurs in verse 20.

These people actually mean to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what they are saying here. They do not want the word of Yahweh to come. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [We do not believe it will ever come]

16.note: Jeremiah uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between what these people are saying about him and what he has actually done. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [However, I did not hasten from being one shepherding following you]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of his work as a prophet as if he were a shepherd **following** Yahweh and caring for his flock. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from caring for your people as you led me]

The implication is that **the disastrous day** is the time when Yahweh will judge the people of Judah. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the day of disaster when you will judge this people]
Here, **my lips** represents what I have said. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what I have spoken]
Here, **your face** represents your presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [it was in your presence]

17.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **terror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Do not terrify me]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a **refuge**, a safe place where someone could go for protection. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are the one who keeps me safe when disaster comes]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **disaster**, you could express the same idea in another way. This also occurs in verse 18. Alternate translation: [when disastrous things happen]

Jeremiah is using **in the day of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “at the time when.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the time of disaster]

18.note: The expression **be put to shame** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Put the ones persecuting me to shame, but do not put me to shame]

Jeremiah is saying what he wants Yahweh to do to **the ones persecuting** him. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [Put to shame the ones persecuting me]

The expression **be dismayed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Dismay them, Yahweh, but do not dismay me]

Jeremiah is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.

19.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **Thus said Yahweh to me** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Yahweh is using **the sons of the people** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the ordinary people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ordinary people]

20.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

22.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **work**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and you are not to labor at anything]
See how you translated this phrase in 11:4.

23.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 7:24.
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:26.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **instruction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and to not accept what I was teaching them]

24.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that kings and officials will enter the gates of Jerusalem if the people obey him and keep the Sabbath day holy. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [And this is what will happen if you listen to me]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **listen** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [if you diligently listen to me]
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8.

25.q: וּ⁠בָ֣אוּ בְ⁠שַׁעֲרֵ֣י הָ⁠עִ֣יר הַ⁠זֹּ֡את מְלָכִ֣ים וְ⁠שָׂרִ֡ים
25.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **kings and officials** before the information about **the gates of this city**. Alternate translation: [then kings and officials shall enter the gates of this city]

Here, **the throne of David** represents the royal authority held by David. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [ruling with the royal authority that David had]

The word **men** is singular in form, but it refers to all the men of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “men.” Alternate translation: [the men of Judah]

26.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people who will come to Jerusalem to worship, not to the kings and officials of the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people shall come from the cities of Judah]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the temple in Jerusalem as if it were his **house**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the temple of Yahweh]

27.note: The pronoun **her** refers to the city of Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then I will kindle a fire in the gates of Jerusalem]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the fire as if it were an animal that could **consume** the palaces of Jerusalem. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it shall completely destroy the palaces of Jerusalem]
See how you translated this expression in 7:20.
